_comment: Committed, reviewed absolute performance floors for the daily perf-regression
compare step (.buildkite/scripts/steps/perf-test-compare.sh). Extracted from
that script's jq so a floor can only be loosened by a reviewed diff, never
quietly inside a shell heredoc. The compare step's rolling median + MAD
absorbs noise; these committed floors are what it cannot normalise a slow real
regression below. See docs/plans/performance-programme.md -> 'Budgets that
ratchet'.
Each budget carries:
dir      'up'   = higher is worse (latency, CPU, heap, alloc, error rate);
'down' = lower is worse (throughput). The compare step applies a
symmetric floor for whichever direction is set.
min_pct  minimum relative move from the rolling median that counts as a
regression when there is no absolute floor (floor == null).
floor    absolute floor: the threshold never crosses this value however
quiet the recent window was. null = no absolute floor (relative
only). For dir 'up' the threshold is max(median+3*sigma, floor);
for dir 'down' it is min(median-3*sigma, floor).
gating   true  = a flagged regression FAILS the build (non-zero exit);
false = reported just as loudly but informational (notify-only)
until the metric earns a history-derived budget.
Wildcard keys 'behaviours.*.<metric>', 'microbench.*.<metric>',
'microbench_extra.*.<metric>' and 'laptop.*.<metric>' apply to every runtime
behaviour / benchmark / laptop-variant key of that shape (e.g. match_http.p95_ms
matches behaviours.*.p95_ms). Every metric a run emits MUST have a matching budget
entry here or the compare step fails closed (a missing budget must not silently
default to 'no floor').
The 'microbench_extra.*' keys are the promoted dark benchmarks (item 15b):
InboundDecode / LocalCallbackDispatch / ForwardPath / OpenApiValidation /
MetricsIncrement (and, from item 16, ResponseWrite). They OMIT 'gating' on
purpose -> non-gating (notify-only): no baseline history yet, so a flagged
regression annotates but must not fail the build. Give them 'gating': true
once each has >=10 clean runs behind it.
The 'laptop.*' keys are the laptop / central-deploy startup + footprint profile
(item 8), emitted by scripts/perf/bench_laptop.py under result.json '.laptop' and
consumed by the daily perf-test-compare.sh. They apply to every '.laptop' variant
key of that shape: laptop.*.ready_ms (docker launch->ready, in-JVM start, and
init-file variants), laptop.*.cold_ready_ms (first-ever in-JVM/init start),
laptop.*.rss_mb + laptop.*.threads (idle footprint at each --memory cap), and
laptop.*.compressed_bytes (image download size). They OMIT 'gating' -> notify-only,
matching item 8's 'notify-only for 10 runs to establish the MAD, then a 25% floor'.
min_pct is 0.25: on a laptop-startup baseline that is a wide dead band (a backstop
against a total AppCDS/warmup loss, NOT a fine regression signal), so the metrics
stay notify-only until >=10 runs of history let a tighter, MAD-derived floor be set.
They ride the FULL baseline (no methodology fingerprint of their own); they are NOT
keyed on the container image digest, which changes on every snapshot rebuild and
would reset the baseline whenever application code changes (the trap the k6 arm-set
fingerprint was chosen over image_digest to avoid).
The 'tls_handshake.*' keys are the TLS/mTLS inbound-handshake cost profile
(item 14), emitted by proxy.js handshake mode under result.json '.tls_handshake'
and augmented with per-handshake server CPU/allocation by perf-test-run.sh. They
apply to every arm key of that shape: tls_handshake.*.handshake_p50_ms +
handshake_p95_ms (TLS handshake time, dir up), tls_handshake.*.delivery_ratio
(throughput/offered — the SCALE-FREE, AUTHORITATIVE keep-up guard, dir DOWN, floor
0.90) and tls_handshake.*.handshakes_per_s (raw achieved rate — dir DOWN, only a
coarse offered-rate-INDEPENDENT liveness floor 1.0, NOT the keep-up signal; see the
dedicated _comment_tls_handshake_rate below), tls_handshake.*.cpu_ms_per_handshake
+ alloc_kb_per_handshake (per-handshake server cost; null on an image predating the
jvm_memory_allocated_bytes metric, so those simply drop out), and error_rate. They
OMIT 'gating' -> notify-only: no baseline history yet, and the numbers vary with the
handshake arm (tls13 < mtls < native-absent), so a flag annotates but must not fail
the build. They ride the FULL baseline (not the k6 arm-set fingerprint) like growth,
since .tls_handshake is not part of .behaviours and the arm set is stable. The 0.25
min_pct on the LATENCY/CPU/alloc metrics (handshake_p50_ms/handshake_p95_ms/
cpu_ms_per_handshake/alloc_kb_per_handshake) is a wide dead band (a backstop against a
gross handshake-cost regression, not a fine signal) until >=10 runs let a tighter,
MAD-derived floor be set. delivery_ratio + handshakes_per_s are the EXCEPTION — they
are absolute floors (0.90 and 1.0), not %-bands (see _comment_tls_handshake_rate
below), and neither is coupled to K6_HS_RATE. NOTE the item
9a forward-proxy arms (forward_absolute_proxy / forward_connect_proxy) land in
.behaviours instead, so they are covered by the existing behaviours.* budgets above
with no new key.
The 'h2_connection_memory.*' key is the HTTP/2 per-connection heap-delta profile
(item 11), emitted by org.mockserver.benchmark.Http2ConnectionMemoryBenchmark and
merged into the result under '.h2_connection_memory' by the h2-multiplex step, keyed
by shape: conn_1x1, conn_10x10, conn_100x10 (N connections x M concurrent in-flight
streams). The figure is bytes_per_connection = (loaded heap - baseline heap) / N, with
the event log cleared before sampling so it measures connection + stream child-channel
state, not logged bodies. dir 'up' = worse (more memory per connection). It OMITS
'gating' -> NOTIFY-ONLY: no run-to-run variance history yet, and the single-connection
(1x1) figure sits at the edge of GC measurement granularity (wide spread), so a flag
annotates but must not fail the build until >=10 clean runs let a MAD-derived floor be
set. The 0.25 min_pct is a wide dead band (a backstop against a gross per-connection
regression, e.g. the class of change the 8.0.0 HTTP/2-multiplex migration warned about,
not a fine signal). DORMANT, like premerge_alloc.* below: the daily perf-test-compare.sh
metrics jq does NOT currently read '.h2_connection_memory' (it is persisted into the S3
run history for a dated trend but not flagged), so this key is unused there today and
CANNOT perturb its fail-closed missing-budget rule. It is committed ready so that when
perf-test-compare.sh gains a '.h2_connection_memory' extraction clause (that script is
owned by the k6/compare unit), the metric resolves to a budget on the first run rather
than reddening the pipeline. The one-time pre-8.0.0-vs-8.0.0 comparison that answers the
changelog is run out-of-band (Docker/RSS, both server versions, identical external
client) and recorded in the item-11 report, not in this rolling budget.
The 'premerge_alloc.*' keys are the PER-MERGE allocation backstop (item 16),
consumed by .buildkite/scripts/steps/perf-alloc-gate.sh — NOT by the daily
perf-test-compare.sh (which never emits a metric of that shape, so these keys
are simply unused there and cannot perturb its fail-closed missing-budget
rule). That gate runs UNCONDITIONALLY in pipeline-java.yml (pre-merge, blocks
the PR) and evaluates each benchmark's gc.alloc.rate.norm (bytes/op) at a
PINNED representative param against an ABSOLUTE floor. It widens the backstop
beyond MatchingBenchmark (matching only) to the request-decode and
response-write paths, so an allocation regression that merely moves bytes out
of the matcher and into decode or the response writer can no longer read as an
improvement.
provisional  true = this floor was NOT derived from >=10 notify-only runs
(median + 3*1.4826*MAD, the programme's budget rule);
there is no history yet for a benchmark just written.
It is instead an absolute bound derived from local
measurement with generous headroom, honestly labelled.
gc.alloc.rate.norm is DETERMINISTIC (allocation is bytes
per op, not timing — it does not depend on CPU speed):
measured error was <0.5% within a JVM and <0.5% across
JVM launches, so a floor at ~+25% cannot false-positive
on noise yet still catches a real regression (e.g. a
re-introduced double body copy, ~+44% at 16 KB — the
exact class of bug InboundDecodeBenchmark guards).
Evidence (2026-09-17, -bm avgt -prof gc -f 1 -wi 3 -i 5, pinned params).
Confirmed in the SAME image the gate uses in CI (mockserver/mockserver:maven,
OpenJDK 17.0.19, amd64 — the CI agents' arch) AND on the arm64 laptop; each
floor is seated on the CONTAINERISED (amd64) figure, since that is where the
gate actually runs:
benchmark              param            laptop(arm64)  container(amd64)  floor
MatchingBenchmark      EXACT/100/INFO   ~1,343,051     1,478,013 B/op    1,850,000 (+25% over container)
InboundDecodeBenchmark bodySize=16384      ~37,520        37,568 B/op       47,000 (+25% over container)
ResponseWriteBenchmark responseSize=16384  ~36,466        36,409 B/op       46,000 (+26% over container)
Decode and response-write reproduced within 0.5% across arch (their alloc is
dominated by the deterministic 16 KB body byte[] copies). MatchingBenchmark
ran ~10% HIGHER on amd64 than on the arm64 laptop, so its floor was RE-SEATED
on the amd64 figure (1,700,000 -> 1,850,000) rather than the laptop one — the
first PR must not be blocked by an arch the floor was never measured on.
GRADUATION PLAN: ResponseWrite is ALSO promoted notify-only into the daily
microbench step (microbench_extra.*), so its history accrues. Once >=10
clean daily runs exist for each of the three, replace each provisional floor
with the history-derived median + 3*1.4826*MAD bound and drop 'provisional'.
Until then these floors gate on the provisional bound (loud, reviewed diff
to loosen), which is safer than a rolling median that would absorb slow
drift — the failure mode item 16 exists to catch.

_comment_info_log_level_arm: Plan open question 5 — the INFO-log-level PUBLICATION arm. perf-test-run.sh
re-measures the two PUBLISHED figure families (the knee curve and the
per-behaviour percentiles) against a SECOND SUT at the SHIPPED-DEFAULT log
level (INFO), so the site can show an honest out-of-the-box number ALONGSIDE
the tracked ERROR baseline. The owner's decision: keep ERROR for the tracked
series (a performance-sensitive user really does set ERROR, and every stored
S3 run is ERROR, so publishing it is legitimate) but publish INFO too, clearly
LABELLED as INFO, so nobody is misled. The INFO figures land under DISTINCT
result keys (.info_log_level_arm.*), so they can never be confused with, or
diffed against, the ERROR series (.behaviours / .sweep / peak_achieved_rps).
The budget keys below MIRROR their ERROR twins but with an info_ prefix, so a
future compare traversal of .info_log_level_arm.behaviours / .peak_achieved_rps
resolves against these — never the ERROR wildcard budgets. They are NON-GATING
(no `gating` key -> notify-only) AND `provisional: true`: plan open question 9
is explicit that a new wall-clock arm ships notify-only, is observed for ten
runs, and only THEN earns a history-derived, possibly-gating budget. NOTE:
perf-test-compare.sh does NOT yet emit metrics under these keys (the INFO
publication is sequenced after a run produces both series); these entries are
staged so the fail-closed missing-budget check is satisfied the moment it does.
info_peak_achieved_rps is dir DOWN (a throughput drop is worse); the INFO
saturation_rps knee is ladder-quantised and recorded but, like its ERROR twin,
NOT budgeted here.
_comment_tls_handshake_rate: WHY keep-up is budgeted on the SCALE-FREE delivery_ratio (AUTHORITATIVE), why
handshakes_per_s is only a coarse liveness floor, and why item 14's recorded
negative control is REFUTED. Measured evidence, Buildkite
mockserver-performance-test build 290, all three arms run in one build:
arm    handshakes_per_s  handshake_p50_ms  cpu_ms_per_handshake
jdk         51.40             6.02              8.9505   (native absent, noOpenSsl)
Item 14's control was worded: 'Force the JDK provider instead of the native one;
the handshake RATE moves.' It does NOT — and structurally CANNOT. proxy.js runs the
handshake arms at a FIXED offered rate (lib/config.js handshakeRate = K6_HS_RATE,
default 50/s) via a k6 constant-arrival-rate executor, and handshakes_per_s is the
completed-iteration rate (1 handshake/iteration). All three arms achieved ~51/s = the
offered rate + measurement jitter, INDEPENDENT of the TLS provider. handshakes_per_s
therefore measures the OFFERED rate, not the server's handshake CAPACITY, and moves
only if the server drops BELOW the modest fixed offered load. The control as worded is
REFUTED: the provider change did not move the rate.
What DID move under the JDK provider — and is the real, sensitive signal — is the
per-handshake COST: handshake_p50_ms 3.992 -> 6.02 (+51%) and cpu_ms_per_handshake
7.133 -> 8.9505 (+25%). Those columns (dir up, 0.25 band above) catch a provider
regression; a +51% p50 move clears the 25% band with margin, and the +25% CPU move
just clears it (so 0.25 is the LOOSEST defensible band for CPU — tighten toward the
history-derived median+3*1.4826*MAD once >=10 runs exist; do NOT widen it).
KEEP-UP (did the server sustain the offered handshake load?) is on delivery_ratio =
throughput/offered, computed per arm by proxy.js. It is INHERENTLY SCALE-FREE: it
sits at ~1.0 whatever the offered rate is, so a change to K6_HS_RATE cannot invalidate
it. That is why keep-up is budgeted HERE and delivery_ratio is the AUTHORITATIVE
keep-up guard: dir down, floor 0.90 (the server must complete >=90% of the offered
handshakes — the exact intent the old '45 out of 50/s' floor encoded, but with the
K6_HS_RATE coupling REMOVED rather than documented). For dir down with a floor the
threshold is min(median-3*sigma, 0.90); with a stable ~1.0 median the operative bound
is the 0.90 floor. build-290 delivery_ratio ~1.03 (cross-arm spread 0.0004 at that one
build — illustrative of how tight this metric sits, NOT the historical per-arm MAD the
threshold actually uses; that MAD will be of the same small order), well clear of 0.90,
so it cannot false-fire on jitter yet fires the moment the server falls below 90% of
offered — proven in the compare replay: candidate ratio 0.80 flags, ~1.0 does not.
handshakes_per_s is DEMOTED to a coarse, offered-rate-INDEPENDENT LIVENESS floor
(dir down, floor 1.0): it fires only if an arm produced <1 completed handshake/sec —
a dead / unreachable SUT — which is true at ANY sane offered rate, so it carries NO
K6_HS_RATE coupling either. It is a defence-in-depth backstop, NOT the keep-up
control: if offered_rps is ever 0/absent, proxy.js emits delivery_ratio = null (it
drops out of the compare via select(.value != null)), and this raw-rate liveness floor
still catches a dead arm. handshakes_per_s is deliberately NOT the authoritative
keep-up signal; do NOT 'promote' it back to a value-of-offered-rate floor (that was
the coupled 45/50 form this change replaced) and do NOT delete delivery_ratio as
'redundant' — delivery_ratio is the one that must survive.
MAINTENANCE: there is NO offered-rate coupling left to maintain. delivery_ratio 0.90
and handshakes_per_s 1.0 are both correct at any K6_HS_RATE, so changing the offered
rate (lib/config.js default, or a .buildkite/scripts/steps/perf-test-run.sh override)
needs NO budget edit here. All tls_handshake.* entries are NON-GATING (no `gating`
key) like the rest of the family: notify-only until >=10 runs of history let a tighter,
MAD-derived floor be set. offered_rps + delivery_ratio are emitted in the
.tls_handshake block for anyone auditing these floors.
_comment_streaming: Item 12 (LLM/SSE streaming). NON-GATING: no history exists yet, and the two
absolute/A-B metrics are measured against a DELIBERATELY CPU- and thread-
constrained SUT so the measurement sits near the knee where a regression shows.
They are therefore RELATIVE tripwires, not absolute production figures.
heap_bytes_per_stream is an UPPER bound - it includes streamed bodies still
retained in the count-bounded event-log ring, not just per-stream state.
_comment_clustered_state: Item 13 (clustered state under load). regression.js is run UNCHANGED against a
single in-memory-backend CONTROL and a two-node Infinispan/JGroups CLUSTER in the
SAME run, both on the same clustered image, and the metric is the per-arm RATIO
(clustered / control). Keyed by arm op (clustered_state.match.p50_ratio, ...). The
ratio is a within-run A/B (the CandidateIndexBenchmark gold standard) that already
cancels host/JVM/GC/image noise, so these ride the FULL baseline in
perf-test-compare.sh — deliberately NOT the k6 arm-set fingerprint and NOT the
image digest (which resets on every snapshot rebuild, the trap the fingerprint was
chosen to avoid). NON-GATING (omit 'gating'): no history exists yet. TWO KINDS of arm
share these keys, distinguished by clustered_state.arms.<op>.crosses_network:
- MEMBERSHIP arms (regression.js: match/forward/template/large..., crosses_network
false) sit near ratio 1.0 — their unlimited-Times matches hit each node's LOCAL
compiled-matcher cache and the event log is node-local, so nothing crosses the
JGroups network per request; the ratio is the steady-state cost of merely being a
clustered member. These MUST NOT be cited as total clustering cost.
- the CROSSING arm (clustered_crossing.js, op `crossing`, crosses_network true) uses
a BOUNDED-Times match whose shared-Times compareAndSet is a synchronous REPL_SYNC
round trip on the cluster (local CAS on the control), so its ratio IS the per-
request network cost item 13 was written to find. p50_ratio is the primary signal (robust at low
N); p95_ratio is present only where BOTH arms cleared MIN_TAIL_SAMPLES.
throughput_ratio is dir:down (clustered slower = lower = worse). 0.25 min_pct is a
wide dead band (a backstop against a gross clustered-overhead regression, not a fine
signal) until >=10 clean runs let a MAD-derived floor be set. The raw per-arm
latencies ALSO land in .behaviours (as <op>_clustered / <op>_clustered_control), so
the behaviours.* budgets above cover them and adding the arms resets the k6 arm-set
fingerprint ONCE (self-healing, notify-only). The genuineness proof (2-node view,
state-crossed-the-network, control-is-single-node) is enforced by the run's
clustered_metrics_present VALIDITY check, not by a budget.
_comment_serving_percore: Item 18 (req/s per core for the SERVING path). lib/perf-percore.sh pins ONE
MockServer SUT to C cores in {1,2,4,8,16} and drives the sweep ladder against
it from a k6 on DISJOINT cores, one point per C under result.json
.serving_percore.points. Keyed serving_percore.<C>c.<metric>, so the wildcard
serving_percore.*.<metric> covers every core-count. They ride the FULL baseline
in perf-test-compare.sh (NOT the k6 arm-set fingerprint and NOT the image digest):
.serving_percore is not part of .behaviours, and the arm set here is the stable
{1,2,4,8,...} core ladder, not the k6 op mix. NON-GATING (omit 'gating'): no
history exists yet, and the figures vary strongly with C and with how many cores
the box could spare the client, so a flag annotates but must not fail the build.
healthy_ceiling_rps  the headline serving figure per C, computed to Finding 1's
definition by REUSING lib/perf-website-figures.jq (fed each
C's sweep as a synthetic run) — not a third copy of the rule.
dir DOWN: a drop in sustainable throughput is worse.
rps_per_core         healthy_ceiling_rps / C — per-core efficiency. dir DOWN.
peak_achieved_rps    max achieved over RIG-VALID rungs (client had CPU headroom,
no dropped iterations, low errors) — the degraded overload
top, same rig-valid peak definition perf-test-run.sh uses.
dir DOWN.
healthy_ceiling_p50_ms  p50 at the ceiling rung (dir UP = worse) — guards that a
throughput hold did not come at a latency cost.
The 0.25 min_pct is a wide dead band (a backstop against a gross per-core
regression, not a fine signal) until >=10 clean runs let a MAD-derived floor be
set. The PRESENCE of the profile when attempted (points-or-skip non-empty) is
enforced by perf-test-compare.sh's serving_percore_attempted gate, not by a budget.
The per-rung ladder, spread, pinning proof (available_processors), skipped rungs
and retention arithmetic are recorded in the artifact but NOT budgeted here.
